nec.stimulus: Counselor: Those who believe that criticism should be gentle rather than harsh should consider the following: change requires a motive, and criticism that is unpleasant provides a motive. Since harsh criticism is unpleasant, harsh criticism provides a motive. Therefore, only harsh criticism will cause the person criticized to change.
nec.questionStem: The reasoning in the counselor's argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that the argument

answerChoices.A: infers that something that is sufficient to provide a motive is necessary to provide a motive
answerChoices.B: fails to address the possibility that in some cases the primary goal of criticism is something other than bringing about change in the person being criticized
answerChoices.C: takes for granted that everyone who is motivated to change will change
answerChoices.D: confuses a motive for doing something with a motive for avoiding something
answerChoices.E: takes the refutation of an argument to be sufficient to show that the argument's conclusion is false

causal.stimulus: People with high blood pressure are generally more nervous and anxious than are people who do not have high blood pressure. This fact shows that this particular combination of personality traits—the so-called hypertensive personality—is likely to cause a person with these traits to develop high blood pressure.
causal.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the ground that the argument

answerChoices.A: fails to define the term “hypertensive personality"
answerChoices.B: presupposes that people have permanent personality traits
answerChoices.C: simply restates the claim that there is a “hypertensive personality” without providing evidence to support that claim
answerChoices.D: takes a correlation between personality traits and high blood pressure as proof that the traits cause high blood pressure
answerChoices.E: focuses on nervousness and anxiety only, ignoring other personality traits that people with high blood pressure might have

part.stimulus: Publishing executive: Our company must sell at least 100,000 books to make a profit this year. However, it is unlikely that we will sell that many, since of the twelve titles we will sell, the one with the best sales prospects, a novel, is unlikely to sell as many as 100,000 copies.
part.questionStem: The publishing executive's argument is most vulnerable to criticism because it overlooks the possibility that

answerChoices.A: the publishing company will sell considerably fewer than 100,000 copies of the novel
answerChoices.B: the publishing company will not make a profit even if it sells more than 100,000 books
answerChoices.C: what is true of the overall profitability of a publishing company is not true of its profitability in a particular year
answerChoices.D: what is true of the sales prospects of the publishing company's individual titles is not true of the sales prospects of the group of titles as a whole
answerChoices.E: the publishing company will sell even fewer books if it does not advertise its books efficiently

unproven.stimulus: Several companies that make herbal teas containing ginseng assert in their marketing that ginseng counteracts the effects of stress. As a result, many people buy these products hoping to improve their health. Yet no definitive scientific study links ginseng with the relief of stress. Thus, these marketing campaigns make false claims.
unproven.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is flawed in that the argument

answerChoices.A: rejects an argument because of its source without evaluating the argument's logical strength
answerChoices.B: concludes that a claim is false merely on the grounds that it has not been shown to be true
answerChoices.C: draws an inference on the basis of a sample that is likely to be unrepresentative
answerChoices.D: fails to address the possibility that many people buy herbal teas containing ginseng because they enjoy drinking the tea
answerChoices.E: fails to address the possibility that some ingredients other than ginseng in the herbal teas containing ginseng counteract the effects of stress

adhom.stimulus: Editorial: The premier’s economic advisor assures her that with the elimination of wasteful spending the goal of reducing taxes while not significantly decreasing government services can be met. But the premier should not listen to this advisor, who in his youth was convicted of embezzlement. Surely his economic advice is as untrustworthy as he is himself, and so the premier should discard any hope of reducing taxes without a significant decrease in government services.
adhom.questionStem: Which one of the following is a questionable argumentative strategy employed in the editorial’s argument?

answerChoices.A: rejecting a proposal on the grounds that a particular implementation of the proposal is likely to fail
answerChoices.B: trying to win support for a proposal by playing on people’s fears of what could happen otherwise
answerChoices.C: criticizing the source of a claim rather than examining the claim itself
answerChoices.D: taking lack of evidence for a claim as evidence undermining that claim
answerChoices.E: presupposing what it sets out to establish

sampling.stimulus: According to the official results of last week's national referendum, 80 percent voted in favor of the proposal. But those results must be rigged. Everyone I know voted against the proposal, which is clear evidence that most people voted against it.
sampling.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately describes a flaw in the reasoning of the argument?

answerChoices.A: The argument uses evidence drawn from a sample that is unlikely to be representative of the general population.
answerChoices.B: The argument presumes the truth of the conclusion that it sets out to prove.
answerChoices.C: The argument rejects a claim by attacking the proponents of the claim rather than addressing the claim itself.
answerChoices.D: The argument fails to make a needed distinction between how people should have voted and how they actually voted.
answerChoices.E: The argument defends a claim solely on the grounds that most people believe it.

appeal.stimulus: Although Jaaks is a respected historian, her negative review of Yancey's new book on the history of coastal fisheries in the region rests on a mistake. Jaaks's review argues that the book inaccurately portrays the lives of fishery workers. However, Yancey used the same research methods in this book as in her other histories, which have been very popular. This book is also very popular in local bookstores.
appeal.questionStem: The reasoning above is flawed in that it

answerChoices.A: relies on the word of a scholar who is unqualified in the area in question
answerChoices.B: attacks the person making the claim at issue rather than addressing the claim
answerChoices.C: takes for granted that the popularity of a book is evidence of its accuracy
answerChoices.D: bases a general conclusion on a sample that is likely to be unrepresentative
answerChoices.E: presumes, without providing justification, that the methods used by Yancey are the only methods that would produce accurate results

circular.stimulus: Cotrell is, at best, able to write magazine articles of average quality. The most compelling pieces of evidence for this are those few of the numerous articles submitted by Cotrell that are superior, since Cotrell, who is incapable of writing an article that is better than average, must obviously have plagiarized superior ones.
circular.questionStem: The argument is most vulnerable to criticism on which one of the following grounds?

answerChoices.A: It simply ignores the existence of potential counterevidence.
answerChoices.C: It presupposes what it seeks to establish.
answerChoices.D: It relies on the judgment of experts in a matter to which their expertise is irrelevant.
answerChoices.E: It infers limits on ability from a few isolated lapses in performance.

contradiction.stimulus: In 2005, an environmental group conducted a study measuring the levels of toxic chemicals in the bodies of eleven volunteers. Scientifically valid inferences could not be drawn from the study because of the small sample size, but the results were interesting nonetheless. Among the subjects tested, younger subjects showed much lower levels of PCBs—toxic chemicals that were banned in the 1970s. This proves that the regulation banning PCBs was effective in reducing human exposure to those chemicals.
contradiction.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument is most vulnerable to criticism on the grounds that the argument

answerChoices.A: takes an inconsistent stance regarding the status of the inferences that can be drawn from the study
answerChoices.B: overlooks the possibility that two or more chemicals produce the same effects
answerChoices.C: concludes that a generalization has been proven true merely on the grounds that it has not been proven false
answerChoices.D: takes something to be the cause of a reduction when it could have been an effect of that reduction
answerChoices.E: does not consider the possibility that PCBs have detrimental effects on human health several years after exposure

equiv.stimulus: Concerned citizen: The mayor, an outspoken critic of the proposed restoration of city hall, is right when he notes that the building is outdated, but that the restoration would be expensive at a time when the budget is already tight. We cannot afford such a luxury item in this time of financial restraint, he says. However, I respectfully disagree. The building provides the last remaining link to the days of the city’s founding, and preserving a sense of municipal history is crucial to maintaining respect for our city government and its authority. So to the question, “Can we really afford to?” I can only respond, “Can we afford not to?”
equiv.questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately characterizes a flaw in the concerned citizen's argument?

answerChoices.A: The argument is solely an emotional appeal to history.
answerChoices.B: The argument ambiguously uses the word “afford.”
answerChoices.C: The argument inappropriately appeals to the authority of the mayor.
answerChoices.D: The argument incorrectly presumes that the restoration would be expensive.
answerChoices.E: The argument inappropriately relies on the emotional connotations of words such as “outdated” and “luxury.”
